Who am I?
I have a twin brother.
I like the fields and hunting.
I am hairy. My brother is Yaakov.
Who am I?
I have a twin brother, too!
At birth, I held his heel.
My name starts with "Y."
What am I?
Eat me with a spoon.
I am red and made with lentils.
Hungry Esav wanted some of me from Yaakov.
Who am I?
I am the twins' mother.
I made delicious food for my husband, Yitzchak.
I helped Yaakov get ready for the bracha.
What am I?
Dig down to make me.
People get water from me.
Yitzchak's servants dug me. No faucet needed!
Who am I?
My father is Avraham.
In my old age, I could not see.
I heard Yaakov's voice, but the hands felt like Esav's.
What am I?
I am special and connected to being the oldest son.
Esav did not value me.
He sold me to Yaakov for food.
What are we?
We came from animals.
Rivkah put us on Yaakov's hands and neck.
We made smooth skin feel hairy.
What are we?
We belonged to the older brother.
The younger brother wore us to see his father.
Rivkah kept us in the house.
Who am I?
My sister is Rivkah.
I live where Yaakov is sent at the end of the parsha.
I am Yaakov's uncle.
What am I?
I am a number connected to Yitzchak's farming.
Hashem blessed his harvest.
"Me'ah she'arim" means this many times as much.
What am I?
I am a well with a name.
Earlier wells caused fights. Nobody fought over me.
My name means there is room: "Hashem made room for us."
Who am I?
I am a king.
I tell Yitzchak to leave because he is so powerful.
Later, I come to make a peace agreement with him.
What am I?
I am part of a bracha.
Find me outdoors early in the morning.
I am moisture from heaven: "tal hashamayim."
Where am I?
Rivkah's brother lives here.
Yaakov is sent here to stay with family and find a wife.
My name is Charan! (Guess before this clue.)
